notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (billing/subscribe product) exploring Redwood for next-gen support agents. Primary goal: replace brittle rule-based flows with a streaming agent that can call Stripe/Zuora and return deterministic JSON payloads for downstream systems.

Context: 250 employees, ~15k support tickets/mo (billing-related ~40%). Platform: React front-end + node backend, payments in Stripe + billing automation in Zuora. Legal requires EU data residency for some marquee customers. IT prefers VPC for Dedicated but happy to start on hosted if SLOs are met.

POC scope: two-week hosted API POC -> measure latency to first token, streaming resilience, tool calling reliability. Agent flows: 1) invoice status + proposed refund, 2) dispute routing (Zuora invoice adjustments), 3) subscription change (apply promo/coupon). Expect structured JSON outputs: {action: refund|adjust|note, amount_cents: int, reason_code: str, ticket_actions: [..]}. SE implemented function calling shim that hits our Stripe lookups via vaulted creds.

Performance requirements: "needs <300ms TTF token for chat agent in common fast-path" (quote from Product Lead: "if customers hang up, we lose revenue"). 95th percentile latency target 400ms end-to-end for simple lookups; more lenient for multi-step flows. Cost sensitivity: mid-market — willing to commit to Dedicated pilot if unit cost drops by 25% vs hosted at current load.

Security/Compliance: running SOC2, require SSO/SAML integration, audit logs for every tool call, optional KMS/HSM for keying. Data residency: EU tenant data must remain in eu-1 region for certain accounts. Legal flagged retention_controls and egress clauses (see drive doc).

Conversation snippets / call notes: - "If streaming degrades, we fall back to synchronous lookup + canned reply" — CS lead. - "Deterministic JSON is must-have for our ticketing pipeline" — Eng manager. - Asked about model drift / regression detection -> Redwood Optimize recommended prompt/eval hooks.

Open questions / Risks: - Hosted API: will streaming + function calls meet latency SLO at scale? (POC metric). - Failure modes: what happens if function call times out? need graceful & auditable fallback. - Pricing: how to price burst capacity for billing season spikes (month end).

Next steps: run POC until 2026-03-16, collect TTF/95p token metrics, present results to procurement on 2026-03-24, SE to prepare Dedicated pilot proposal if POC meets latency & cost thresholds.
